name: Pravo Horo
desc: The most widespread Bulgarian line dance, in straight 2/4 (2+2) and danced across the whole country with countless regional variants. Even pulse with the low tupan 'dum' on the downbeat.

name: Shopsko Horo
desc: A fast, energetic men's dance from the Shopluk region around Sofia in straight 2/4, full of small shaking footwork (natrisane). Even meter with strong downbeat accents.

name: Pajdushko Horo
desc: A limping dance in 5/16 grouped quick-slow (2+3); the uneven step gives it its characteristic hobble. The long group head falls on pulse 2.

name: Chetvorno Horo
desc: A Shop men's dance in 7/16 grouped slow-quick-quick (3+2+2); the long beat leads each measure. Group heads at 0, 3 and 5.

name: Rachenitsa
desc: The Bulgarian national dance in 7/16 grouped quick-quick-slow (2+2+3), the long beat ending each measure. The defining solo and wedding rachenitsa rhythm.

name: Trakiiska Rachenitsa
desc: The Thracian variant of rachenitsa in 7/16 (2+2+3), broader and more grounded than the Shop version, with the long beat closing each bar.

name: Daichovo Horo
desc: A lively northern Bulgarian line dance in 9/16 grouped quick-quick-quick-slow (2+2+2+3), the long beat last. Group heads at 0, 2, 4, 6.

name: Svornato Horo
desc: A four-phrase Pirin line dance in 9/16 (2+2+2+3) sharing daichovo's meter, with the slow beat closing each measure.

name: Grancharsko Horo
desc: The 'potter's dance' in 9/16 grouped quick-slow-quick-quick (2+3+2+2); the long beat sits second, distinguishing it from daichovo. Group heads at 0, 2, 5, 7.

name: Dospatsko Horo
desc: A Rhodope line dance in 8/16 grouped slow-quick-slow (3+2+3), with long beats framing a short middle group. Heads at 0, 3 and 5.

name: Gankino Horo
desc: A northern Bulgarian dance in 11/16 grouped 2+2+3+2+2, the long beat in the centre. Same meter as kopanitsa; the third group of three is the rhythmic pivot.

name: Kopanitsa
desc: A fast Shop/Thracian dance in 11/16 grouped quick-quick-slow-quick-quick (2+2+3+2+2), with the slow group at the centre. Group heads at 0, 2, 4, 7, 9.

name: Bistrishka Kopanitsa
desc: The Shop village variant of kopanitsa from Bistritsa in 11/16 (2+2+3+2+2), driving and percussive with the central long beat.

name: Krivo Plovdivsko Horo
desc: A 'crooked' Thracian dance in 13/16 grouped 2+2+2+3+2+2, the long beat fourth. Group heads at 0, 2, 4, 6, 9, 11.

name: Eleno Mome
desc: A widespread Bulgarian song-dance often realised in 13/16 grouped 2+2+2+3+2+2; the long beat sits fourth before the closing pair of duples.

name: Petrunino Horo
desc: A Shop dance in 13/16 grouped 2+2+2+3+2+2, related to krivo plovdivsko, with the long group in the fourth position.

name: Buchimish
desc: A Shop showpiece in 15/16 grouped 2+2+2+2+3+2+2; the single long beat (fifth group) is the only triple among duples. Group heads at 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 11, 13.

name: Yove Malaj Mome
desc: A Shop dance in 18/16 built as 7+11, i.e. (3+2+2)+(2+2+3+2+2), joining a chetvorno head to a kopanitsa tail. Heavy 'dum' on each half (0 and 9).

name: Sandansko Horo
desc: A long Pirin compound dance in 22/16 grouped 2+2+2+3+2+2+2+3+2+2, two slow beats anchoring the two halves. Group heads at 0,2,4,6,9,11,13,15,18,20.

name: Sedi Donka
desc: The longest Bulgarian aksak, Plovdivsko horo in 25/16 built as 7+7+11 = (3+2+2)+(3+2+2)+(2+2+3+2+2). Three 'dum' anchors at 0, 7 and 14.

name: Ramo Ramo
desc: A Pirin/Macedonian-style line dance in 11/16 (2+2+3+2+2), kopanitsa meter, with the long beat at the centre of the bar.

name: Lesnoto
desc: The 'easy' Macedonian line/song dance (also Pravoto/Lesno) in 7/8 grouped slow-quick-quick (3+2+2); the long beat opens each measure. Heads at 0, 3, 5.

name: Maaaško Lesnoto
desc: A men's lesnoto in 7/8 (3+2+2) with weightier, grounded steps; the leading long beat carries the heavy stamp.

name: Kalajdzisko Oro
desc: The 'tinsmith's dance' from the Veles region in 7/8 grouped 3+2+2 like lesnoto, with intricate ornamented footwork on the leading long beat.

name: Sadi Moma
desc: A Macedonian song-dance in 7/8 grouped slow-quick-quick (3+2+2), the long opening beat carrying the vocal phrase head.

name: Ratevka
desc: A dance from Ratevo (Maleshevo) usually in 7/8 grouped 3+2+2, often paired with Berovka in a medley; the long beat leads each bar.

name: Tresenica
desc: A 'shaking' women's dance from the Mariovo region; in its rachenitsa-type form it sits in 7/8 grouped 2+2+3 with the long beat closing the bar.

name: Devetorka
desc: A Macedonian dance in 9/8 grouped quick-quick-quick-slow (2+2+2+3), the daichovo meter; the closing long beat marks the phrase end. Heads at 0, 2, 4, 6.

name: Devojce Devojce
desc: A Macedonian song-dance in 9/8 grouped quick-slow-quick-quick (2+3+2+2); the long beat sits second. Group heads at 0, 2, 5, 7.

name: Postupano Oro
desc: A heavy, 'stepped' men's dance from the Skopje region in 12/8 grouped 3+2+2+3+2, framing two short groups between long beats. Heads at 0, 3, 5, 7, 10.

name: Berance
desc: A stately Macedonian men's dance in 12/8 grouped 3+2+2+3+2; the two long beats anchor the slow, broad steps. Group heads at 0, 3, 5, 7, 10.

name: Pusteno
desc: The 'released' Macedonian line dance in 12/8 grouped 3+2+2+3+2, akin to berance, with broad swaying steps on the two long beats.

name: Kutsano Oro
desc: A 'limping' Macedonian dance in 12/8 grouped 3+2+2+3+2, sharing the pusteno/berance meter with a hobbling accent on the long beats.

name: Acano Mlada Nevesto
desc: A Macedonian song-dance in 9/8 grouped 2+1+2+2+2; an irregular short second group gives it its distinctive lilt. Heads at 0, 2, 3, 5, 7.

name: Cucuk
desc: A Macedonian/Roma dance in 9/8 grouped slow-quick-quick-quick (3+2+2+2), the long beat leading. Group heads at 0, 3, 5, 7.

name: Dolgoto Oro
desc: The 'long dance' in 12/8 grouped 2+2+3+2+3, with two long beats spacing the duple groups. Heads at 0, 2, 5, 7, 10.

name: Osumnaestorka
desc: The 'eighteen' dance in 18/8 grouped 2+2+3+2+2+3+2+2, two long beats splitting the measure into mirrored kopanitsa-like halves. Heads at 0,2,4,7,9,11,13,16.

name: Kolo
desc: The Serbian national circle dance in straight 2/4 ('dvojka'), danced in a closed circle with intricate footwork. Strong downbeat 'dum' driving the pulse.

name: Uzicko Kolo
desc: A fast, energetic kolo from Uzice in western Serbia in 2/4, one of the most popular Serbian dances with quick hopping steps over a driving even pulse.

name: Moravac
desc: A smooth, flowing kolo from the Morava valley in 2/4, slower and simpler than uzicko, a favourite for festive gatherings with an even, walking pulse.

name: Cacak
desc: A ten-measure Serbian kolo in 2/4 from the Cacak region, with a fixed pattern of steps over a steady even beat. Strong downbeat accent each bar.

name: Makedonka
desc: A Serbian kolo in 2/4 with a Macedonian-flavoured melody, danced in the standard closed-circle kolo style over an even duple pulse.

name: Zikino Kolo
desc: A popular Serbian kolo (U sest, 'in six') in 2/4 with a six-measure step pattern, danced widely at celebrations over a steady even beat.

name: Geamparale
desc: A Dobrujan chain dance in 7/16 grouped short-short-long (2+2+3), the Romanian cognate of rachenitsa with the long beat closing each bar.

name: Sarba
desc: A fast Romanian/Moldavian chain dance in 2/4, danced in a line with hands on shoulders over a driving even pulse with the 'dum' on the downbeat.

name: Hora
desc: The Romanian national circle dance, commonly in a slow 6/8 grouped 3+3, danced in a closed circle with measured swaying steps. Accents on the two group heads.

name: Briul pe Sase
desc: A men's belt dance 'on six' in 2/4 (six pulses, 2+2+2) with brisk stamping footwork. Group heads on each duple at 0, 2, 4.

name: Invartita
desc: A Transylvanian couple turning dance, here in a 6/8 (3+3) realisation; partners spin to measured beats. Strong 'dum' on each group head.

name: Ca la Breaza
desc: A Muntenian dance 'in the style of Breaza' in 10/16 grouped 2+3+2+3, alternating short and long groups. Group heads at 0, 2, 5, 7.

name: Kalamatianos
desc: The Greek national line dance (syrtos in 7/8) grouped slow-quick-quick (3+2+2), three steps per bar with the long beat leading. Group heads at 0, 3, 5.

name: Syrtos
desc: The 'dragging' Greek circle dance in even 4/4, sharing kalamatianos steps but in straight meter; smooth, flowing line dance over an even pulse.

name: Ballos
desc: An island couple dance (Aegean) in a flowing even 2/4, danced as a courting dialogue between partners over a steady pulse.

name: Tsamiko
desc: A heroic mainland men's dance in 3/4 (here a 6-pulse 3+3 grid), danced in an open circle with a W-hold and dramatic dips on the strong beats.

name: Zeibekiko
desc: An improvised solo rebetiko dance in 9/8, commonly grouped 2+2+2+3 with a slow, swaying emotional pulse; the closing long beat carries the weight. Heads at 0,2,4,6.

name: Karsilamas
desc: A face-to-face couple dance in 9/8 grouped 2+2+2+3, lively and flirtatious, with the final long beat closing each phrase. Group heads at 0, 2, 4, 6.

name: Hasapiko
desc: The 'butcher's dance' in its fast 2/4 form, a line dance with hands on shoulders; the basis of sirtaki, driven by a steady even pulse.

name: Hasaposerviko
desc: The fast 'Serbian-style' hasapiko in 2/4, a brisk line dance reflecting Balkan influence, with the 'dum' on the downbeat of an even meter.

name: Pentozali
desc: A vigorous Cretan war dance in 2/4 with high leaps and improvisation, accelerating from a moderate to a fast even pulse. Strong downbeat accent.

name: Sousta
desc: A bouncy Cretan/Dodecanese couple dance in 2/4, its springy steps mirroring the 'sousta' (spring); danced over a lively even pulse.

name: Ikariotikos
desc: A fast line dance from the island of Ikaria in 2/4, accelerating to a frenzy with quick side steps over a driving even pulse.

name: Antikristos
desc: A face-to-face Anatolian-Greek couple dance of the karsilamas family in 9/8 grouped 2+2+2+3, with the closing long beat ending each phrase.

name: Sirtaki
desc: A 20th-century stage dance combining slow hasapiko and fast hasaposerviko, in 4/4 then 2/4, accelerating over an even pulse with the 'dum' on the downbeat.

name: Pravoto
desc: The Macedonian 'straight' song-dance (local name for lesnoto) in 7/8 grouped 3+2+2, the long beat opening each measure. Group heads at 0, 3, 5.
